---
title: "Logistic regression"
---

**Question:** among men who received blood transfusions
during radical prostatectomy,
is the storage age of the transfused red blood cells
associated with prostate cancer recurrence?
([Cata et al., 2011](https://higgi13425.github.io/medicaldata/reference/blood_storage.html))

Recurrence is a yes/no outcome,
so we use logistic regression
and report odds ratios.
This section follows the
[analysis](https://ds4biomed.tech/analysis-intro.html) and
[tidymodels](https://ds4biomed.tech/machine-learning-tidymodels.html) chapters
of *Data Science for the Biomedical Sciences*.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(medicaldata)
```

We'll start from `blood`,
which you made in the
[Coded variables](02-clean-and-tidy.qmd#exercise-2-coded-variables) exercise.
The code below makes it again,
so this page works on its own.
The outcome must be a factor,
and its second level (`yes`) is the event the model predicts.

```{r}
blood <- blood_storage |>
  mutate(
    recurrence = factor(Recurrence, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes")),
    rbc_age_group = factor(RBC.Age.Group, levels = 1:3,
                           labels = c("younger", "middle", "older"))
  )
```

## Exercise 1: Fit a logistic regression

Logistic regression models the log-odds of the event:

$$
\log\left(\frac{p}{1 - p}\right) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_1 + \dots
$$

where $p$ is the probability of recurrence.
Exponentiating a coefficient, $e^{\beta}$, gives an **odds ratio**.

::: {.callout-note}
## Your turn

1. Before we model, let's look at the outcome.
   Plot the proportion of men with a recurrence in each storage-age group
   as stacked bars (`geom_bar(position = "fill")`).
   Does recurrence look different between the groups?
2. Fit a logistic regression of `recurrence` on `rbc_age_group`.
3. Show the odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals.
4. What group are the odds ratios compared with?
   Is older stored blood associated with recurrence?

```{r}
#| eval: false
ggplot(blood, aes(x = ____, fill = ____)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill")

rec_fit <- logistic_reg() |>
  fit(____ ~ ____, data = blood)

tidy(rec_fit, exponentiate = ____, conf.int = ____)
```
:::
